name: MonarchShiftRoster
title: ShiftRoster
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.PrimaryScrollableTabRow and Tab (one day or one person at a time), androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu with DropdownMenuItem and RadioButton (the cell menu), androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll with CollectionInfo semantics (the grid), MonarchEventChip, MonarchAvatar, MonarchBadge, MonarchSkeleton, MonarchBanner, MonarchEmptyState, android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: Who works which shift on which day: a shift, a day off or nothing for each person and day of a range, with hours per person and the number of people working per day, edited from a menu on each cell.
whenToUse: For a team's weekly or fortnightly rota in a workforce or attendance screen, where a manager assigns shifts and reads coverage per day. Save each MonarchShiftRosterChange as it arrives.
whenNotToUse: For meetings or appointments use MonarchAgendaList or a calendar time grid. For one person's own upcoming shifts use MonarchAgendaList. For bulk rotations or copying a week, build the product's own dialog; the roster edits one cell at a time.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun MonarchShiftRoster(members: List<MonarchShiftRosterMember>, shifts: List<MonarchShiftRosterShift>, from: Long, value: Map<String, Map<Long, MonarchShiftRosterAssignment>>, onValueChange: (Map<String, Map<Long, MonarchShiftRosterAssignment>>, MonarchShiftRosterChange) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, days: Int = 7, layout: MonarchShiftRosterLayout = MonarchShiftRosterLayout.Automatic, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, loading: Boolean = false, showTotals: Boolean = true, today: Long? = System.currentTimeMillis(), timeZone: String? = null, is24Hour: Boolean? = null, error: String? = null, onMemberClick: ((MonarchShiftRosterMember) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchShiftRosterLabels = MonarchShiftRosterLabels(), empty: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)
class MonarchShiftRosterShift(id: String, name: String, start: Int, end: Int, shortName: String? = null, color: Color = Color.Unspecified)
class MonarchShiftRosterMember(id: String, name: String, description: String? = null, image: Painter? = null)
sealed interface MonarchShiftRosterAssignment { class Shift(shiftId: String); data object Off }
class MonarchShiftRosterChange(memberId: String, day: Long, assignment: MonarchShiftRosterAssignment?)
enum class MonarchShiftRosterLayout { Automatic, Grid, ByDay, ByPerson }

class MonarchShiftRosterLabels(roster: String? = null, person: String? = null, day: String? = null, off: String? = null, unassigned: String? = null, clear: String? = null, menuTitle: ((name: String, day: String) -> String)? = null, cell: ((name: String, day: String, assignment: String) -> String)? = null, range: ((start: String, end: String) -> String)? = null, overnight: String? = null, hours: String? = null, hoursValue: ((hours: String) -> String)? = null, working: String? = null, workingValue: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, today: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyDescription: String? = null, loading: String? = null)

options.name: members
options.description: The people in display order, each with an id, a name, an optional description line and an optional picture Painter.

options.name: shifts
options.description: The shifts in menu order: id, name, start and end in minutes from midnight (an end at or before the start ends the next day), an optional short name for the grid and an optional color.

options.name: from
options.description: The first day shown: any time on that date in UTC, as epoch milliseconds (a day key).

options.name: value
options.description: Assignments by member id, then by day key: Shift(shiftId) or Off. A missing day is not assigned.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the whole new value and the one change (member, day, new assignment or null when cleared).

options.name: days
options.description: How many days to show from from, 1 to 62.

options.name: layout
options.description: Grid (people by days), ByDay (tabs of days, a row per person), ByPerson (tabs of people, a row per day), or Automatic: the grid when every column fits and the font scale is at most 1.3, otherwise ByDay.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the cells can be used, for example false while saving. Tabs keep working.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Shows the assignments as text without menus.

options.name: loading
options.description: Shows a skeleton placeholder, read as "Loading roster", instead of the roster.

options.name: showTotals
options.description: Shows each person's hours over the range and the number of people working per day.

options.name: today
options.description: Any time on the day marked Today, read in timeZone; null for no marker. The day layout opens on it when it is in the range.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone today is read in. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: is24Hour
options.description: Shows shift times on a 24-hour clock. null follows the device's 24-hour setting.

options.name: error
options.description: A message shown in a danger MonarchBanner instead of the roster.

options.name: onMemberClick
options.description: Makes each person a button, for example to open their schedule on a detail screen.

options.name: empty
options.description: Replaces the built-in empty state shown when members is empty.

states.name: shift
states.description: A MonarchEventChip bar in the shift's color with the name (the short name in the grid) and the times.

states.name: off
states.description: A muted fill with the word Off.

states.name: not assigned
states.description: A dashed outline with "Not assigned" (a dash in the narrow grid cells; TalkBack still reads "Not assigned").

states.name: today
states.description: Today's tab reads "Today" above the date, the day heading and grid header use the strong accent and an info badge or the word Today.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A Material 3 DropdownMenu headed by the person and the day, with a radio item per shift, Off, and Clear when the day is assigned.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Cells keep their look but cannot be pressed; TalkBack reads them as disabled.

states.name: loading
states.description: A skeleton placeholder replaces the roster.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger banner with the app's message replaces the roster.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no people, an empty state (or the app's empty slot) replaces the roster.

appearance: Rows are separated by the default divider; names are in the default text color and descriptions, hours and counts in the muted color. A shift cell keeps the event chip's colors (the shift color only as the bar and a light tint), a day off uses the muted background, and an unassigned day a dashed default border. Today uses the strong accent and an info badge. The grid's header and footer rows sit on the subtle background. High contrast themes use their own roles; every state is also written.
platformNotes: The web ShiftRoster is always a table of people by days with a roving-focus keyboard grid and Delete to clear. On a phone that table does not fit, so Android shows one day at a time with Material 3 tabs (or one person at a time) and keeps the table for wide windows (Automatic picks it when every column fits). The web takes ISO dates and a BCP 47 locale and hour cycle; Android takes day keys in epoch milliseconds, the configuration's locale and the device's 24-hour setting. Assignments are a sealed MonarchShiftRosterAssignment (Shift or Off; a missing day is not assigned) because Kotlin cannot tell undefined from null. The value is controlled only (no defaultValue), as for every Monarch component. The plan's drag to assign is not offered: the web has no drag either, and a menu per cell is the touch and TalkBack pattern. There is no iOS ShiftRoster yet, so the names follow the web. Experimental because it is a product pattern not yet adopted by a Rook Android app.
accessibility: Each editable cell is one button with a 48dp touch target, named "<person>, <day>: <assignment>", for example "Alex Kim, Monday, November 2, Today: Morning, 06:00 to 14:00"; an overnight shift adds "overnight" and a grid cell with a short name adds it after the full name.

The cell menu is a Material 3 DropdownMenu headed by a heading with the person and the day; the current choice is marked selected and has a filled radio button, and each shift is read with its spoken time range.
Read-only cells are one text element with the same name and no click action; disabled cells are read as disabled.
Day tabs are Material 3 tabs read as the full date, with "Today" for today; the selected tab is marked selected. The tab rows are named "Day" or "Person".
The day's date is a heading, and the number working is a polite live region, so TalkBack says the new count after an assignment.
Each person is one element read as "name, description, Hours: total"; with onMemberClick it is a button with a 48dp target.
The grid is a collection named "Shift roster"; each cell carries its row and column, day headers are headings read as the full date, and footer counts are read with the date.
Avatars are decorative; no state is shown by color alone.
From font scale 1.5 the cell moves under the person so no text is cut.
edgeCases: Day keys in value may be any time on the date in UTC; they are matched by date, and a change replaces any key of that date.
An assignment to a shift id that is not among shifts reads as not assigned and counts no hours.
A shift whose end equals its start lasts 24 hours.
Hours are rounded to one decimal in the locale's number format.
The roster does not scroll vertically; put it in a scrolling screen. The grid scrolls sideways when forced on a narrow window.
Long names and descriptions wrap; nothing is truncated.

examples.title: Editable week
Read only, one person at a time, with a week toolbar
examples.setup:
var week by remember { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
val from = 1_793_577_600_000L + week * 7 * 86_400_000L
examples.code:
Column {
    MonarchCalendarToolbar(
        title = "Week ${week + 1}",
        view = MonarchCalendarToolbarView.Week,
        onToday = { week = 0 },
        onPrevious = { week -= 1 },
        onNext = { week += 1 },
        previousIcon = { Icon(SampleIcons.ChevronLeft, contentDescription = null) },
        nextIcon = { Icon(SampleIcons.ChevronRight, contentDescription = null) },
    )
    @OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
    MonarchShiftRoster(
        members = listOf(MonarchShiftRosterMember("a", "Alex Kim")),
        shifts = listOf(MonarchShiftRosterShift("e", "Evening", start = 14 * 60, end = 22 * 60)),
        from = from,
        value = mapOf("a" to mapOf(from to MonarchShiftRosterAssignment.Shift("e"))),
        onValueChange = { _, _ -> },
        days = 3,
        layout = MonarchShiftRosterLayout.ByPerson,
        readOnly = true,
        today = null,
    )
}

parityExceptions.reason: An unassigned cell is drawn as a dash, and its button is named for TalkBack with the person, the day and "Not assigned" ("Sam Lee, Wednesday 4 November: Not assigned"), not with the dash alone.
parityExceptions.convention: a control is named by what it does and where, not by its glyph (Material accessibility)
